review_scope: Complete73-line article and eight-line model exclusion reusable read, including all36 candidates, context, metadata, expiry comments, staged activation, feature exceptions, enterprise/org delegation and model exclusions. Prior default-availability reusable not duplicated. No current external activation, target settings, omission/rendering assurance, adopted policy or rights clearance.

claims.statement: Default-availability article scope is Business/Enterprise with the Copilot cloud feature declaration; not proof of target entitlement.
The default-policy reusable distinguishes separate GA feature and model defaults; previously fully reviewed dependency is not duplicated.
Editorial expiry comments surround a temporary activation notice; source maintenance metadata is not an executable or contractual instruction.
The pin says the new-feature default policy is configurable but not yet active, with activation scheduled for October 22, 2026; no current runtime state is verified.
The activation notice covers new and existing unconfigured GA features; a banner counts eligible unconfigured policies for impact assessment.
The pin describes the feature-default policy as enabled by default, automatically enabling unconfigured features on October 22 without action; effective target settings must still be observed.
Feature-default scope distinguishes new GA features, preview-to-GA transitions and existing GA features whose settings are Unconfigured.
New generally available features are within the described feature-default scope.
Features moving from preview to general availability enter the described feature-default scope.
Existing GA features are covered only when Unconfigured; explicit decisions are distinct.
At enterprise level, the feature-default applies to features labeled Unconfigured.
At organization level, the feature-default applies only when the enterprise delegates and the organization has not explicitly configured the feature.
Preview features are excluded from the feature-default policy until the applicable GA transition.
For this default policy, feature scope includes policies on the enterprise Features & clients page; page existence alone is not configured enforcement.
Code-review policy on the Agents page is also within the described feature-default scope.
Copilot MCP servers policy on the MCP page is also within the described feature-default scope.
The default-policy feature set has explicit exceptions; do not include every policy in a generic auto-enable evaluator.
Data-residency/FedRAMP restrictive model policies are excluded from the feature-default mechanism.
Store local sessions in the Cloud for CLI and VS Code is excluded from the feature-default mechanism.
The pin describes released-model default availability as active for new and unconfigured GA models; this remains a source declaration.
The included model-exclusion fragment supplies required exceptions and default delegation labeling; it is independently reviewed in this batch.
Disabling default policies can disable automatic enablement at enterprise or applicable organization scope; reading this procedure is not authority to change it.
An explicitly disabled feature/model is ineligible for automatic enablement even if the corresponding default policy remains enabled.
Feature and model configuration procedures are separate linked dependencies; organization policy procedure is already reviewed, other links are not certified here.
The source recommends monitoring releases/GA announcements via changelog to choose settings; release awareness is not current effective-policy proof.
Unconfigured models carry Delegate to Default Policy in enterprise or organization settings; label visibility does not establish actual configuration.
A newly released model inherits the default until explicitly configured, subject to the exclusion list.
Excluded model categories are disabled by default regardless of the model-default setting; this is not a ban on separately approved manual enablement.
Pre-GA models are excluded from default-model enablement.
Open-weight models including DeepSeek and the named Kimi model variables are excluded from default-model enablement.
Models outside GitHub's described data-retention agreement, including the named Fable variables, are excluded from default-model enablement.
When enterprise models are restricted to data-resident or FedRAMP-compliant models, nonconforming models are excluded from default enablement.
